title: Color as Emotional Expectation
definition: Color establishes an emotional expectation before the audience evaluates content. Its effect depends on context, proportion, contrast, culture and repetition; no isolated color carries one universal emotion.
diagnostic_method: Map dominant, supporting and accent colors
Test the palette in the real channel and cultural context
observable_indicators: Dominant color matches the intended emotional posture
analysis_questions: What should the audience feel before reading?
Does the palette preserve meaning in the target culture and medium?
decision_rules: Evaluate color as a system, never as an isolated swatch
Reject palettes whose emotional effect contradicts the declared positioning

good_examples.situation: A financial report uses restrained dark neutrals with one controlled signal color
good_examples.result: The hierarchy feels precise and risk-aware

bad_examples.situation: Every campaign uses a different saturated palette

limits_and_counterexamples: Accessibility and contrast requirements take precedence
expected_result: Color choices create a consistent, testable emotional expectation across touchpoints.

relationships.justification: Controlled color hierarchy contributes to perceived coherence and authority.

forbidden_uses: Treating the candidate as approved canon
Using it as evidence of a real-world fact without an external source

review_note: Aprobado por el fundador para el canon piloto Entity Bible v2.
